page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features a 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced hardware extensions, including AVX-512 (VNNI, BF16) and Intel AMX instructions (tile and int8) for accelerated vector and matrix mathematics.

A defining aspect of the E64-32s_v6 is its memory density. Equipped with 512 GB of RAM, the system maintains a 16 GB per vCPU ratio, offering substantial headroom for memory-bound applications without requiring the compute overhead of a full 64-vCPU host. In synthetic and platform benchmarks, memory bandwidth performance ranks in the top quartile, achieving 246.92 GB/s in large-block read operations and 141.39 GB/s in write operations. The architecture also records strong multi-core Geekbench results (17,375) and high decompression throughput, while general multi-core stress testing and database execution align within median performance percentiles.

Because the E64-32s_v6 does not bundle local ephemeral storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, all persistent data depends entirely on external Azure managed disks via its Premium Storage interface. This decoupled architecture presents a deliberate hardware tradeoff: lower local disk wear and flexible storage tiering, balanced against reliance on networked storage for disk I/O. The provisioned hardware profile delivers high resource density for workloads constrained by database licensing costs or memory boundaries, making the instance well-matched for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise enterprise resource planning platforms, and large-scale data analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, the instance provides 512 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive 16 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware platform incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache as well as Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets for accelerated matrix and vector processing. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 246 GB/s on reads alongside solid Geekbench multi-core performance. The instance provides no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating remote managed disks for all persistent volume needs. This resource configuration yields optimal qualitative cost efficiency for systems bound by software licensing fees that require massive memory footprints, such as enterprise in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and data analytics engines.
